description: Three sample and hold sections that each sample a signal on a clock, or make a fresh random voltage per channel when nothing is patched to sample

params.text: Sets one end of the range the random voltages cover, a whole number from -10V to 10V; whichever of the two knobs is lower becomes the bottom
Sets the other end of the range the random voltages cover, a whole number from -10V to 10V; whichever of the two knobs is higher becomes the top
Sets how many polyphonic channels this section puts out, 1 to 16; at 0 it follows the cable patched to the section instead
Sets the chance that a channel takes a new random voltage on each clock pulse, 0 to 1; a channel that loses the roll keeps the voltage it had
Rounds this section's output to the nearest semitone
Samples once, as a rising edge at this section's clock jack does

inputs.text: The signal to be sampled; leave it unpatched and this section makes random voltages instead
A rising edge samples the signal, or makes a fresh random voltage when nothing is patched to sample

outputs.text: Carries the held voltages, one per channel, until the next clock pulse

notes: the bottom section has no settings of its own; its range, channel count, probability and quantise all come from the middle section's controls
a section with nothing patched to its signal jack is a random voltage source, and one with a signal patched is a sample and hold
a clock cable's polyphony is summed to one voltage before it is read, so every channel of a section is sampled at the same moment
the probability applies only when a section is making random voltages; with a signal patched every clock pulse samples it, despite the README saying otherwise
the quantise switch rounds a sampled signal as well as a generated voltage, despite the README saying it applies only to generated CV
a section writes nothing to its output until a clock is patched or its button is pressed
